_horizon_simulated._note: THE HORIZON IS SIMULATED UNDER THE INVITE LINE. `SimParams.invite_optin_rate` is drawn per mint as a Bernoulli at `optin_rate_drawn`, all-or-nothing at `max_count` (the checkout fills all 3 recipients or the mint sends none, so a count sampled over 0..3 would model a control that does not exist), from a DEDICATED RNG stream -- so a run with the line off shares this one's realised history exactly, mint for mint, and only the money differs. `optin_rate_realised` is the share the draw actually produced and is a measurement; `optin_rate_drawn` is the ASSUMPTION it was drawn from and is not. `ton_deducted_over_the_horizon` is the summed seventh line over the run, and it is TON that left the residual -- so `final_state`, the floor appreciation, the kill criteria and the genesis blocks are now measured WITH the line, not above it. `mean_pool_injection_ton_measured` is the mean residual in TON, not a rate: it equals mean beta only because every mint in this run prices at MINT_PRICE = 1 TON, which is why it is comparable against `beta_table`'s rows at all.

k_lt_1_check._note: The ratchet theorem never used beta being constant: for any injection I > 0 and any k < 1, (T+I)/(S+kI/p_f) > p_f. A smaller beta shrinks injection and rebate TOGETHER, in the same ratio -- which is what `emission_tracks_injection` checks numerically. The single K_CEIL clamp sits on the SUMMED UPLIFTS and is not a function of beta at all (D-101, 'why no invariant moves').

tribute.divisor_weight_formula: w(p) = e * p**0.5, with s = floor(sqrt(p)) submitted and verified s^2 <= p < (s+1)^2
tribute.flat_dividend_accrual: div_acc += f * 0.10 / pi(n) per mint; entry[p] stamped at mint; claim pays div_acc - entry[p]
tribute.prime_mint_tribute: the whole 10% line has no recipient on a prime mint and falls to the pool (SS4.1, SS4.2.1)

rebate._k_on_prime_mint_note: SS5.1/SS11.15 is CLOSED: primes emit nothing, k = 0 unconditionally. There is no k = k_min fallback and none should appear in the contract.
rebate._S_MAX_source: DECISIONS.md D-156 -- OWNER-SET, not sim-selected, exactly as D-154's `genesis_donation_ton` is. The sim CONSUMES this figure and re-derives the emission curve, the floor and every dependent block from it; it does not choose it. 1,200,000,000 PRIMES was set at 100x the then-12,000,000 genesis supply; D-166 moved S0 to 11,000,000 and left S_MAX where the owner set it, so it is no longer a multiple of S0 and nothing reads it as one. SS5's emission is multiplicative (`dS/S = k*beta/T`), so `S` is bounded iff `k` is integrable in `u = ln n`; `2.7/log10(n)` is not, and `K_MIN = 0.2` flattens it entirely past n = 10^13.5. D-156 does NOT replace that curve -- it multiplies it by `(S_MAX - S)/S_MAX`, which makes emission logistic and bounds `S` without touching the sim-calibrated shape where the game lives. `k` only shrinks, so `k < 1` and the ratchet theorem strengthen.
rebate._newcomer_source: OWNER-SET incumbent pair, NOT swept. Opened by the recruit edge in primes_ledger.tolk (a gift mint to an address minterState has never seen) and spent one per clocked mint. DECISIONS.md D-106.

flush._sandwich_note: Re-measured WITH the guard. The v4 file's number was measured against storeCoins(1) -- no guard at all -- and is not carried forward. D-190 (2026-09-26): the attacker is now also the flush CALLER -- it pumps up to 8x the flush, then sizes the tranche to the pumped pool (D-143), which the earlier model (flush sized before the pump, pump capped at 0.5x) could not do and so read 0.00 TON. The PnL here is BURN EFFICIENCY lost while the market is under the floor: the ratchet still never averages above p_f, and T, S and p_f do not move.

pending_growth._note: Under the floor guard a fill requires the market to be at or below the floor. In a market that stays above it, `pending` is not a backlog: it is the protocol's standing bid, and it counts in T either way (SS5).

pending_growth_above_floor_market._note: Under the floor guard a fill requires the market to be at or below the floor. In a market that stays above it, `pending` is not a backlog: it is the protocol's standing bid, and it counts in T either way (SS5).

staked_reserve._fraction_definitions: `staked_fraction` is the share of the ratchet's whole obligation (`pending + stakedCost + exiting`) that ends up in tsTON; `reserve_fraction_of_pending` = 1 - it is the liquid share, and is the one `reserveTarget` multiplies on chain. Both are `flush_pct` (0.20) times the swept `reserve_days` below: reserve = flush_pct * N, staked = 1 - flush_pct * N.
staked_reserve._reserve_days_ceiling_note: A day count above 4 is not a bigger reserve, it is NO STAKING: at flush_pct = 0.20 the reserve reaches the whole obligation at N = 5, and every N at or above it stakes exactly zero. The 1..14 sweep therefore has only 4 distinct outcomes, which is the strongest reason the constant is published as a fraction.
staked_reserve._source: The RATCHET's TON reserve staked as tsTON (CONCEPT.md SS4.3.2, DECISIONS.md D-151) -- UNRELATED to the top-level `staking` block, which is D-168's PRIMES staking paid from the treasury vest. Different asset (TON, not PRIMES), different actor (the ratchet contract, not a player), different section. sim/scripts/run_phase1.py staking_report, seed=20260814, STAKING_PLAN.md P1. `staked_fraction` comes from the SMALLEST N in 1..14 with zero unmet flush demand in the base three-year run and <= 1% of demand unmet in the `pending_growth_above_floor_market` stress run; `stake_min_ton` is the larger of the two implied minima below, rounded up to a 1/2/5 figure. WHAT THIS RUN DOES NOT SHOW: the base run produced ZERO exits at EVERY N -- the venue-depth clamp keeps a real tranche two orders of magnitude below the ceiling the reserve is sized against, so the reserve was never drawn on and the stress scenario never flushes at all. The three exit legs are therefore UNEXERCISED by this sweep, and a zero here is an absence of evidence, not a pass: leg 1, leg 2 and leg 3 are proved only by the mock pool's branch tests (STAKING_PLAN.md P0 point 1), and `unmet_flush_ton == 0` must not be quoted as a measurement of them.
staked_reserve._exit_slippage_bps_source: OWNER's value, 2026-09-20 (DECISIONS.md D-151 point 5), NOT a sim output. A stable pool charges 0.04% and fills inside ~10-20 bps, so 50 bps clears a thin book without being a real haircut and refuses in a genuine depeg. The sim CONSUMES it -- every leg-2 fill is modelled at the full bound, so `realized_slippage_ton` is the worst case this number permits, never an average.
staked_reserve._harvest_interval_source: OWNER's value, 2026-09-20 (DECISIONS.md D-151 point 4): >= 30 days apart. 2592000 = 30 * 86400.
staked_reserve._harvest_dust_source: DERIVED, not picked: 20 x the gas cost of ONE jetton transfer at basechain config 21. `jetton_wallet.transfer` (5923) + `jetton_wallet.internal_transfer` (5840) = 11763 gas units over 2 transactions, from contracts/gas-baseline.json, priced by sim/primes_sim/gas.py's `gas_to_ton` at 0.000797534 TON; x20 = 0.015950681. Below this a harvest costs more gas than it moves value, so it is skipped (D-151 point 4). Every run in the sweeps below harvests on this threshold, and none of them is affected by it: a month's accrual at the modelled stake sizes is three orders of magnitude above it, so it guards the empty-pool case and nothing else.
staked_reserve._modelled_apr_source: ASSUMPTION, NOT MEASURED -- the same standing as `invites.optin_rate_assumed`. Tonstakers' realised APR is an external number with no measurement in this repo, so it is SWEPT over [0.02, 0.04, 0.06] in `apr_sweep` rather than chosen, and 0.04 is used as the headline for the `reserve_days` and `stake_min_ton` selections above. Yield never enters `T`, so the APR feeds back into nothing: every other figure in this block is identical at all three rates.

reserve_days_sweep._rule: smallest N with unmet_flush_ton == 0 in the base run AND unmet_share_of_demand <= 0.01 in the stress run
reserve_days_sweep._leg_assumption: Both legs of the sweep run with `leg2_fill_prob = 0` -- the DeDust leg unavailable, every leg-1 miss becoming the ~36 h payout bill. That is the only reading under which the rule can discriminate: with leg 2 available every exit is instant, so `unmet_flush_ton` is identically zero at every N by construction. It is a bound, not a measured refusal rate.

stake_min_sweep._rule: one constraint, rounded up to a 1/2/5 figure: cumulative flat fees <= 10% of cumulative accrued yield at the headline APR. It is 1/x in the minimum, so each row extrapolates to the value that would just satisfy it (`implies_min_from_fee_share_ton`) and the largest extrapolation is taken, over rows with at least 10 stakes -- fewer is a timing, not a flow. A second constraint -- round trips must not outpace the ratchet's own gas accrual (RATCHET_HOP_GAS) -- was DELETED by D-146 (2026-09-22): the pool's flat fees are paid by the caller of `stake`/`unstake`, not out of that accrual, so there is nothing for it to bound. It never bound: fee share implied 289.4 TON against its 117.6.

The head walks composites; a prime opens a Dutch lot as the head passes it, so the head never parks and there is no prime-head dwell to measure. (Until 2026-09-24 this block carried the legacy model's dwell distribution, stall alert, sensitivity sweep and stall-sized prime-quest budget; all four measured a deleted risk and are deleted with it.)

prime_lane_model._source: determinations.d20_baseline.prime_lane_model_fed_to_engine, measured by sim/scripts/run_determinations.py (market.evaluate_lane). The premium splits per D-114: the ratchet's half is the figure above.

score._formula: D(n) = clamp(LEN + max(DIGIT) + LIFE + sum(FORM) + CULTURE + POSITION, 0, SCORE_MAX). LEN pays LEN_W*(LEN_REF - digits) while digits < LEN_REF; the six DIGIT patterns take a MAX because they imply one another; everything else sums. SCORE_MAX = 87 IS owner answer 9's 420 TON ceiling: the ladder tops out at MINT_PRICE * 2^(87/10) = 415.9 TON.
score._weights_provenance: OWNER-DECLARED (D-99 SS1.3, owner answers 3/6/10 signed 2026-09-04). The sim does not fit these and must not be read as having chosen them (CLAUDE.md rule 3). They are parsed out of shared/opcodes.ts's SCORE_BITS/SCORE_TERMS at generation time so the sim, the contract and the webapp cannot drift. What the SIM owns is the distribution they induce (`histogram`) and the two rebate rates that distribution sizes (genesis.score_rebate).

_score_consumers.p0: P0(n) = max(LOT_FLOOR, MINT_PRICE * 2^(D(n)/SCORE_HALVING), 1.5*NPV(n) if prime) -- trophy_auction.price_map
_score_consumers.rebate: REBATE_PER_POINT * D(n) on a head-minted composite -- genesis.score_rebate
_score_consumers.min_bid_increment: a step function of D(n)//SCORE_HALVING -- acquisition.bid_increment_ladder

rebate_family._note: p > 100,000 and p = 1 (mod 101). D-99 strips this family of its rarity meaning: it is not a bit, it adds no points and it lifts no price. It selects a REBATE and nothing else.

histogram._max_score_note: REALISED maximum over this window, not the clamp. The clamp is SCORE_MAX = 87, which IS owner answer 9's 420 TON ceiling: MINT_PRICE * 2^(87/10) = 415.9 TON on the shipped ladder. Only a number that is rare in three ways at once reaches it, which is answer 9 as a measurement rather than a claim.

res_gas_derivation.rule: D-90: RES_GAS = the settle hop that rides to the ledger with the close + the TVM compute of the close/settle pair, rounded up to the next 0.005 TON, and then FLOORED AT 0.07 TON (D-90.4, raised by D-113). It is CARVED FROM THE WINNING BID.
res_gas_derivation._retained_note: D-90.4 retains the pre-D-90 RES_GAS so no price moves. Instant settlement is cheaper than the claim it replaced, so the fee now over-collects by 0.035 TON per won lot. That is published rather than banked: it is a real surplus and a candidate for the next re-derivation, not a hidden margin. Lowering it is a PRICE change (LOT_FLOOR = MINT_PRICE + RES_GAS) and therefore an owner decision, which is why this run does not take it.
res_gas_derivation._scoring_left_note: The worst-case scoring row (`market.reserve.max_digits`) is DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Under D-33 `D(n)` is evaluated at `open_lot` to quote P0 and the bid increment, and the opener pays for it in their own message. Carrying it inside RES_GAS would charge the winner for compute the opener already paid.

inputs._substitution_note: none -- every row is measured under its own name
inputs._source: hop value mirrors primes_market.tolk SETTLE_GAS and primes_ledger.tolk handleSettle; gas from contracts/gas-baseline.json.

off_head.res_gas_note: SS4.4: RES_GAS is carved from the winning bid before the premium is computed and funds the lot's mint IN THE CLOSE TRANSACTION. It is NEVER waivable, NEVER payable in PRIMES, and NEVER routed anywhere but settlement. DERIVED as a floor and RETAINED at 0.07 by D-90.4/D-113 (see `retained_headroom_ton`): must match RES_GAS in primes_market.tolk.

import_window._rule: W = max(ceil(peak_head_advance_numbers * safety / 256) * 256, 4096), where peak_head_advance_numbers is the most numbers the base run's head covered in any sliding window of keeper_outage_tolerance_days. A head that reaches importedTo*256 before an import lands stalls (mints refund) until anyone calls import_block -- a stall, never corruption -- and W costs W/256 ledger words, so it is sized generously.
import_window._source: sim/scripts/run_phase1.py import_window_report over the baseline Engine's mint_log (DECISIONS.md D-196, GAUNTLET.md V30.1).
import_window._flush_window_note: D-198 reuses W as the flush window (primes_ledger.tolk walkLimitN: the walk stops W blocks past Aux.unsoldFlushed). Same stall, same derivation: flush_unsold is due once the head leaves a block, so with the keeper live the cursor trails the head by <= 1 block and an outage leaves W blocks of head travel before mints refund -- the lower bound this rule sizes. The other side, rows held on the ledger, is not a sizing input: a full W-block window holds 857 unsold rows with forfeit rows (measured, LotBlock.spec.ts), far under config 43's 65,536 cells.

inputs._keeper_outage_tolerance_note: DESIGN INPUT, not a sim output: the keeper (KEEPER_INTERVAL_MS = 60 s) may be down this long before the head can stall.

naming._note: D-212 replaces D-179's PRIMES burn (and deletes primes_sink.tolk): the CURRENT OWNER of a minted number names it for a TON fee sent to the collection's `name_number`; the fee is forwarded to the ledger as `royalty_to_ratchet`, a pure floor step. Both fees are deploy data on the collection (the rename fee also on the registrar, for an era trophy's paid re-engraving), with no setter.
naming._name_fee_rule: the first naming of a number. TON figure = name_fee_eur at the TON/EUR rate on genesis day, passed as PRIMES_NAME_FEE_TON; no default exists, and a genesis without it fails
naming._rename_fee_rule: every later naming of the same number, by whoever owns it then, and every era-trophy engraving after its free first one. PRIMES_RENAME_FEE_TON may lower it on testnet only
naming._invariant: a naming fee raises T by exactly the fee and leaves S untouched (SS5); every refusal refunds the whole payment

trophy_auction._declared_note: SCORE_HALVING, PRIME_P0_MULTIPLE, AUCTION_WINDOW and BID_EXTENSION are DECLARED, the same way genesis.prime_dutch_lane's DECAY_SECONDS and PRIME_P0_MULTIPLE are declared: owned by the owner, with a stated constraint each, and NOT simulation outputs. Nothing in run_phase1.py fits them and TROPHY_AUCTION_PLAN.md SS6 is explicit that they must not be dressed as derived. Post-launch they become calibratable against realised clearing prices; pre-launch they cannot. What IS derived here: the FRAC table, the RESERVE_FLOOR identity check (RESERVE_FLOOR itself is DERIVED, = MINT_PRICE + RES_GAS), the openable-lot counts and the NPV(p) ladder. The MIN_INCREMENT rule has LEFT this list: D-33 makes it a sim output and acquisition.bid_increment_ladder owns it.

constraints.RESERVE_FLOOR_TON: DERIVED, not declared. Must equal MINT_PRICE + RES_GAS exactly (D-30/D-37 deleted the RES_PRIORITY_BASE term); checked in reserve_floor_identity below.
constraints.SCORE_MAX: 87 (D-99, owner-declared). The ONE clamp on the summed categories, and it IS owner answer 9's 420 TON ceiling: the ladder tops out at 2^(87/10) = 415.9 TON.
constraints.AUCTION_WINDOW_SECONDS: 7 days (D4). The mint happens at head arrival regardless, so the window costs nothing; shorter weakens discovery, longer holds bid capital for no gain.
constraints.BID_EXTENSION_SECONDS: 67 minutes (D10), applied as closesAt = max(closesAt, now + BID_EXTENSION). Admissible range ~30 min (a bidder in any timezone can respond) to ~2 h (the lot terminates); anything in that band satisfies the constraint, so the free choice is spent on a prime that belongs to the project. 67 is prime, and the choice is deliberate.

price_map._rule: P0(n) = max( MINT_PRICE * 2^(D(n)/SCORE_HALVING), PRIME_P0_MULTIPLE * NPV(n) if n prime, RESERVE_FLOOR ). D(n) is D-99 33-category additive score, clamped once at SCORE_MAX = 87 -- see the `score` block.
price_map._integer_rule: P0 = (MINT_PRICE_NANOTON << (D / SCORE_HALVING)) * FRAC[D % SCORE_HALVING] >> 16, with FRAC[j] = round(2^(j/SCORE_HALVING) * 2^16). One shift, one lookup, one multiply, one floor-divide -- exact integer arithmetic on TVM. It runs on the AUCTION contract, not on reserve(), so it does not touch SS4.4 point 1's 0.0002 TON scoring headroom.

frac_table_approximation._note: The FRAC table rounds 2^(j/10) to 16 fractional bits, so the shipped ladder differs from the true exponential by at most 2^-17 relative (~7.6e-6). At the SCORE_MAX rung that is a few tens of milliTON on a 4,096 TON opening bid. Stated rather than absorbed into a tolerance: the contract and the sim agree to the nanoton on the SHIPPED expression, and the shipped expression is this close to 2^(D/10).

_rule.prime: descending Dutch lane, openable BEFORE its turn at a flat P0(p); the decay clock starts at its turn and terminates at exactly MINT_PRICE (D-31)
_rule.composite: ascending auction lane, at any D(n) -- opening the lot IS a paid first bid at P0(n), 7-day clock, D-8 anti-snipe extension, and the won lot becomes a claim that waits for the head and never expires (D-30)
_rule.primorial: neither; mint at the head only (CONCEPT.md SS7)

lane_entry._one_route_rule: CONCEPT.md SS4.4 superseding box: there is exactly ONE route to a number ahead of the head and it depends only on primality. The `D(n) >= D_MIN` gate, the flat-fee `Reserve` entry points and `RES_PRIORITY_BASE` are all deleted.
lane_entry._quoting_consequence: The lane a number belongs to depends on primality, so getIsOpenable(n) must run Miller-Rabin itself rather than trusting a caller-supplied kind. SS4.4 point 1a's cleanest property -- one price query taking one argument -- is spent here, deliberately.

reserve_floor_identity._rule: RESERVE_FLOOR = MINT_PRICE + RES_GAS, exactly (D-30 deleted RES_PRIORITY_BASE).

bounds._note: P0 is weakly monotone in D(n) by construction (the RESERVE_FLOOR branch is a constant floor under a strictly increasing ladder), and strictly monotone above the score at which the ladder clears the floor. Under D-99 the SCORE_MAX rung is not a guard but THE STATED CEILING: 2^(87/10) = 415.9 TON, which is owner answer 9's 420 TON cap expressed as a clamp on the score rather than as a second rule. `declared_band_at_score_max_ton` is that ceiling with the FRAC table's rounding allowance, and it is what FuzzInvariants.spec.ts's `ladder(87) <= 420.5 TON` asserts.

openable_lots._note: D-30 drops the `D(n) >= D_MIN` gate: any reservable composite may be opened as an ascending lot, up to D-11's 14-digit AUCTIONABLE_MAX. `historical_thresholds` is what the gate used to exclude, kept so the size of the change is a published number rather than an impression. Exhaustive over [10^2, 10^7), from score.histogram.

npv_ladder._purpose: D3. The engine NPVs stop at 13 and 17 is the first number that needs it. NPV/sqrt(p) runs 583, 312, 167, 116, 73, 62 over p = 2..13 -- declining fast and not a clean function of sqrt(p) -- so no cheap extrapolation is available and the table is GENERATED by the analytic sweep rather than fitted.
npv_ladder.npv_branch_binding_rule: 1.5 * NPV(p) > max(LOT_FLOOR, MINT_PRICE * 2^(D(p)/SCORE_HALVING)), evaluated per prime. D-99 deletes PRIME_P0_MIN, so the old flat threshold_ton = PRIME_P0_MIN / PRIME_P0_MULTIPLE (10/3 TON) is gone with it.
npv_ladder._bound_note: The dictionary carries the first 2000 primes. That bound is not a size guess: under D-99 the NPV branch of P0 binds only where 1.5 * NPV(p) beats the prime's OWN ladder price max(LOT_FLOOR, 2^(D(p)/10)), which is true for 555 primes and last true at p = 6577. Everything past that is headroom against a longer horizon or a lower discount rate. Beyond the dictionary the contract falls back to the ladder and quotes exactly the same price it would have quoted with the entry present. PRIME_P0_MIN, the old third branch and the old flat 10/3 TON threshold, is deleted.

npv_calibration._finding: DIFFERENT COMPUTATIONS, NOT A BUG, AND NOT RECONCILED AWAY. The six engine NPVs (by_prime.*.engine_npv_ton) come from the ENGINE run (analysis.discounted_tribute_npv_by_prime over the realised mint log, wall-clock discounting). The trophy ladder uses the ANALYTIC sweep (tribute.prime_tribute_npv, mint-index clock at a constant rate) because that is the only one that generalises past 13. At the engine's own horizon and realised mint rate the analytic sweep sits a few percent ABOVE the engine on all six, with a spread of well under one percentage point -- a level offset, not a shape disagreement. genesis._donation_vs_modelled_depth: HONEST MODELLING GAP, flagged rather than buried. `genesis_seed_ton` (200) is a NOMINAL that sizes S0 = seed * L * (1/2 + vault_pct) = 11,000,000 PRIMES (D-166) and the depth of the DeDust pair the agent loop trades against; `genesis_donation_ton` (132.50) is the TON actually credited into `T`. Before D-100 these were the same number by construction (D-92 chose the donation to reproduce `seed / S0`), so the modelled pool and `T` coincided. They no longer do, and D-140 moved the real pair AGAIN, and D-154 resized it a third time: it is now 1,312,854 PRIMES, all minted by the donation (D-166 took the operator's 250,000 first vest tranche out with the operator lock), against 14.13 TON, priced at `primes * p_f`. D-154 NARROWS this gap without closing it -- 14.13 TON of real pair against depth sized off a 200 TON nominal is the same order of magnitude for the first time, where D-100 point 2's 0.1022 TON was three orders below it. Neither number is the point: what D-140 fixed is the RATIO, which is the only thing about the pair the protocol can see. Re-sizing the modelled pool is still NOT done, because pool depth feeds k_max calibration, the reserves and the kill criteria, and silently re-deriving those off an operational choice is exactly the drift CLAUDE.md rule 3 forbids. MEASURED 2026-09-18 (GAUNTLET.md X14, docs/audit/x14-modelled-pool-depth.md): one full run with the pool seeded at the real pair, against the committed run, moves 45 numeric leaves and NOT ONE of them is a parameter. `rebate` (k_max_cap, K_CEIL, PRIME_UPLIFT and every uplift tier) and `off_head` (RES_GAS, LOT_FLOOR; then named `reservations`) are byte-identical, and all three kill criteria keep `passed: true`. So the re-sizing is NOT adopted, and this is now a measured statement rather than an open question. The finding worth carrying: the unguarded sandwich control goes from 10.70% to 99.9999% of swapped value extracted, so SS4.3.1's floor guard is MORE load-bearing at the real depth, not less. What follows from the change that WAS made: `market_over_floor_at_open` is 1.0 -- not D-92's 6x and not D-100's unintended 286x -- so the SS4.3.1 floor guard is live from the first mint instead of refusing every attempt.

rebate_family._density_argument: D-96, unchanged by D-99's narrowing. Dirichlet's theorem makes the class infinite and equidistributed: exactly 1/phi(101) = 1 in 100 primes at every depth, so it is never exhausted -- the reason D-96 replaced D-68's closed 25-member family. The owner's declared ceiling is 1 in 1,000 INTEGERS; the sieved density above is what this window actually realises.

projection._includes_auction_path: YES, and that is D-99 SS5 point 4's correction to this block. Every rebate-family prime inside the horizon is counted whether it mints at the head or at auction, because the family rebate pays on either route. Counting it at the head-arrival floor is the conservative direction only for the head route; an auction win claims earlier, at a LOWER floor and therefore more PRIMES, which the 50% headroom is there to absorb.

worst_case._meaning: The theoretical ceiling if every member claimed at the GENESIS floor, which cannot happen once the head has moved. It exists to size the claim-time clamp (payout_formula), not the track balance.

treasury._why: D-100 point 6. vesting._release_rule: Release is a TARGET, total_amount * unlocked / tranches, and a call transfers the difference against what has already gone out -- never a fixed per-tranche amount. vesting._invariant: The lock touches NO economic state. S counted the whole allocation at genesis (SS3.3) and does not move; T never saw it. p_f = T/S is identical with and without this contract -- the vest changes who can sell and when, never anybody's floor.

treasury._governance_note: D-100 point 8 as amended by D-167, D-194 and D-173's 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-21 amendments: a proposal transfers {TON | PRIMES | tsTON} to an address (LP is NOT proposable, D-167) or confirms a queued venue change (D-194, moves no value). Execute is permissionless after close for one more vote length, and a bounced execute is re-executable. Point 10b is accepted in writing: with no quorum a single 30-day locker passes a proposal unless someone with more weight votes no. No standing operator position exists (D-166), so the defences are rules: the 25% cap, the notice plus the vote (two days in total, not per proposal -- D-130), and the 1% proposer threshold. distribution_rate_selection.criterion: Pay stakers 50% of the treasury's free PRIMES in the first year, so the pot pays out at roughly the pace the treasury's 1,000,000-PRIMES vest funds it (four tranches over 270 days). Stated BEFORE the number: `P = 1 - (1 - share)^(1/365)`.
distribution_rate_selection._epoch_rule: A permissionless `distribute()`, at most once per `epoch_seconds`, sends `budget = free * rate * epoch / (10000 * 86400)` PRIMES to the stake contract, which streams it linearly over the next epoch. `free` is the treasury's whole PRIMES balance -- nothing accrues inside the treasury any more.
distribution_rate_selection._never_empties: `budget = P * free` is a fraction of a BALANCE, so the pot decays geometrically and is positive for every finite t. prime_prefunding_displacement._source: sim/scripts/run_determinations.py -> market.prime_prefunding_displacement. LANE-AWARE BUYER MODEL: an interested buyer of prime p arrives while p is ahead of the head, tau days before its turn (tau = composites between HEAD_LO and p over the engine's realised composite mints/day), with the lane model's private value (P1 scarcity value of the number + P2 NPV/uplift/rights, P4 lognormal sigma). They open the ascending lot now iff (v - P0)*(1 - exp(-lam*s*tau)) > P0*(exp(r*tau) - 1): certainty against a rival taking the descending lot at its opening price P0, against the carry of paying tau days early (a prime earns no tribute before the head passes it). s = P(value >= P0); r = the tribute NPV's discount rate. P(displaced) = 1 - exp(-lam * integral of P(open | tau)), exact for Poisson arrivals. ASSUMED, NOT MEASURED: (1) buyer interest ahead of the head arrives at the same per-prime rate lam as on the descending lot (P3/P6), swept 0.005..0.30/day because no lot has ever run; (2) the buyer is myopic -- rivals are the Poisson future, earlier waiters are invisible on chain; (3) CONSERVATIVE (pushes displacement UP): opening ignores rivals contesting the ascending lot, waiting ignores buying below P0 as the descending lot decays. The P0 sweep multiplies the shipped P0(p) = max(ladder, RESERVE_FLOOR, 1.5*NPV) as a whole. `lane_unaware_upper_bound_share` is the composite lane's own rule (every buyer valuing it >= P0 opens).
